All 9 tests pass (both test files). Changes, all in `reports/render.py`:

- **Added `csv` renderer.** Header row then data rows, using the stdlib csv writer so cells containing commas or quotes are quoted correctly.
- **Added `html` renderer.** Heading, table, one `th` row, one `td` row per data row, closing tag, each on its own line. Cell text and the title are HTML-escaped, which the tests don't exercise but avoids broken markup for values like `<`.
- **Added `render_many`.** Validates the format once up front so an unknown format raises before any report is rendered, then maps `render` over the list.
- **Dropped the trailing newline from `render`.** The batch test expects an exact `"B\n\n1"`. That exposed that the text format is really title, blank line, then rows, so with no rows it still ends in a blank line. Renderers now return the finished string instead of a line list so the text format can express that directly.

result:
All 9 tests pass (both test files). Changes, all in `reports/render.py`:

- **Added `csv` renderer.** Header row then data rows, using the stdlib csv writer so cells containing commas or quotes are quoted correctly.
- **Added `html` renderer.** Heading, table, one `th` row, one `td` row per data row, closing tag, each on its own line. Cell text and the title are HTML-escaped, which the tests don't exercise but avoids broken markup for values like `<`.
- **Added `render_many`.** Validates the format once up front so an unknown format raises before any report is rendered, then maps `render` over the list.
- **Dropped the trailing newline from `render`.** The batch test expects an exact `"B\n\n1"`. That exposed that the text format is really title, blank line, then rows, so with no rows it still ends in a blank line. Renderers now return the finished string instead of a line list so the text format can express that directly.
